title: The Excellence of an Army
note: The army, which wealth provides and which wins victories, takes two chapters. This first one is on what makes an army good.

couplets.plain: A complete army that fears no wound and wins is the first of all a ruler’s riches.
couplets.pm: An army complete in its four parts, elephants and the rest, which doesn’t fear being hurt in battle and beats the enemy, is the chief of all a ruler’s riches. If it feared wounds it couldn’t win. It guards the other parts of the state and the ruler himself, so it comes first.

links.quote: the first of all a ruler’s riches
links.reason: Ranks a complete, winning army first among all a ruler owns.
Asks of that army above all that it fear no wound.
Tells a ruler which of his riches counts for most.

couplets.plain: The hard courage that fears no wound when the fight goes badly, even when the force is worn down, is rare except in an old army.
couplets.pm: When the ruler is hard pressed in battle, the hard courage to stand and take the blows without fear, even when reduced to a few, is found only in the army that has come down from his ancestors. Of the six kinds of army, hereditary, hired, country, forest, allied and enemy, the hereditary is the best, so the ruler should reward it well.

links.quote: hard courage that fears no wound
links.reason: Prizes the hard courage that holds on when the fight goes badly.

links.quote: rare except in an old army
links.reason: Singles out the old army as the only one that can do it.

couplets.plain: What if a host of rats roars like the sea? A cobra breathes, and they are gone.
couplets.pm: What harm if an enemy of rats roars like the sea? When the cobra merely breathes, they perish. Many who aren’t warriors may gather and shout, but a warrior doesn’t fear them, and when he stirs they perish. One warrior is better to have than many who aren’t.

links.quote: A cobra breathes, and they are gone

couplets.plain: An army is what doesn’t fall, can’t be turned by treachery, and has hard courage handed down.
couplets.pm: A ruler’s army is what doesn’t perish in battle, isn’t subverted by the enemy, and has courage come down from of old. Not perishing shows valour and honour. Not being subverted shows loving-kindness for the ruler.

links.quote: doesn’t fall, can’t be turned by treachery, and has hard courage handed down

couplets.plain: An army is what has the strength to stand together and face even Death, coming on in rage.
couplets.pm: An army is what has the strength to stand with one heart and hold out, even if Death himself, for whom there is no cure, comes on in rage. So many hearts are one because of loving-kindness for the ruler. Strength here is strength of mind.

links.quote: stand together and face even Death

couplets.plain: Valour, honour, walking the noble path and clarity of mind: these four alone protect an army.
couplets.pm: These four alone protect an army: fierce courage, honour, going the good way past heroes went, and being trusted by the ruler. By them, in turn, it kills enemies quickly, keeps the ruler from harm, doesn’t strike at the backs of the fleeing, and can’t be subverted. Enemies don’t come near such people, so they need no other defence.
couplets.note: தேற்றம் can mean clarity or trust. He takes it as the ruler’s trust in the army.

links.quote: these four alone protect an army
links.reason: Names what protects an army: valour, honour, the noble path and clarity of mind.
Valour comes first among the four protections of an army.
Honour stands beside valour among the four protections of an army.
Clarity of mind is counted among the four things that protect an army.

couplets.plain: An army knows how to bear the battle that comes at it, holds back the vanguard and goes forward.
couplets.pm: Knowing the formation that counters the enemy formation coming against it, an army draws itself up, stops their vanguard reaching it and advances on them. Formation has seven parts, four kinds and thirty varieties, all set out in the northern books.

links.quote: holds back the vanguard and goes forward
links.reason: Makes going forward the mark of an army, since it knows how to bear the fight that comes.

couplets.plain: Even without the power to strike or the strength to hold, an army gains greatness from how it looks.
couplets.pm: Even if an army lacks the fierce courage to go and kill the enemy and the strength to bear attack, it gains greatness by its splendid appearance. “Even if” shows these can’t really be done without. The splendour is adorned chariots, elephants and horses with banners, flags, parasols, instruments and horns. The greatness is that enemies fear it at first sight.

couplets.plain: An army wins if it has no shrinking, no grudge that won’t go, and no poverty.
couplets.pm: An army beats the enemy if it doesn’t shrink in number, has no lasting resentment and isn’t poor. Desertion, and poverty among those who stay, come from a ruler who doesn’t give wealth. Lasting resentment comes from his seizing their women or shaming them. Where these exist they have no loving-kindness for him and won’t fight hard.

links.quote: no shrinking, no grudge that won’t go, and no poverty
links.reason: Victory rests on three things: no shrinking, no lasting grudge and no poverty.

couplets.plain: An army may have plenty of steadfast men, but without leaders it is no army.
couplets.pm: An army may have many warriors who stand firm in battle, but without warrior leaders it won’t stand. If its commanders don’t hold but run, it won’t fight, since no one is left to see it, and it will run too.

links.quote: without leaders it is no army

links.reason: Makes the leader the one person an army can’t do without.

ideaLinks.quote: without leaders it is no army
ideaLinks.reason: Without leaders, steadfast men however many are no army.
